newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 -private.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest direct hogs steady-off $0.50 -private.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hogs early Friday sold steady to $0.50 per cwt lower, pressured by thin demand from packers planning light Saturday slaughter, livestock dealers and packer buyers said.

Saturday hog slaughter was estimated at 20,000-23,000 head versus 21,000 a week earlier and 6,000 a year ago, livestock analysts said. Slaughter was seen light as packers continue to fight unprofitable margins by trimming kills, sources said.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hogs sold $0.50 per cwt lower at $56.50-$57.00 in the country and up to $58.50 at plants, sources there said.
Illinois hogs sold $0.50 lower in light activity, with $57.00 to $58.00 paid in the country and $58.50 to $59.00 at plants, dealers there said.

Indiana hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower also in light trading, with a top of $57.00 reported in the country and $59.00 at plants. Several packer buyers reported being out of the market after buying hogs they needed on Thursday for Friday operations.
Ohio hogs sold steady to $0.50 lower at $55.00 to $56.00 in the country and $56.00 to $57.00 at plants.
